generators.carrier: map from presented inscriptions to the distinctions the regime has (internal classes, quotient by ≈ₙ)
append token a to an inscription, e.g. <> to <a>

relations.statement: Under the opaque convention q(x)=q(y) iff x ≈ₙ y; internal identity is the quotient P/≈ₙ, and q(<a>)=q(<>)
relations.hypotheses: Opaque identity convention (assumption); O_0 = O_1 = empty so no internal observation separates <a> from <>

lemmas.statement: There exist x,y in P with x ≠ y and q(x)=q(y): presentation difference does not imply internal difference (witness x=<>, y=<a> under the opaque convention)
lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem pres_not_internal : ∃ (P N : Type) (q : P → N) (x y : P), x ≠ y ∧ q x = q y := ⟨Bool, Unit, fun _ => (), true, false, by decide, rfl⟩

lemmas.statement: Equal q-values do not imply equal inscriptions: q(x)=q(y) does not imply x=y (same witness)
lemmas.lean_skeleton:
theorem q_eq_not_eq : ¬ (∀ (P N : Type) (q : P → N) (x y : P), q x = q y → x = y) := by
  intro h
  have := h Bool Unit (fun _ => ()) true false rfl
  exact absurd this (by decide)

near_misses.claim: Under exact-inscription convention <a> is a new internal state, so presentation gain equals internal gain
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Target holds only under the opaque convention; the statement is conditional and this convention is a different assumption

near_misses.claim: No new presentation implies no new distinction of any kind, e.g. empty vs nonempty payload
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Bottleneck: a regime can gain a syntactic distinction without assigning a referent; this claim is about discriminating power
